The benchmark contains one run for each eval/configuration pair. The reported standard deviations describe differences among the four evals, not repeat-run variability, so this dataset cannot establish flakiness or run-to-run stability.

The inspect_capabilities/runtime-authority expectation fails in both configurations for evals 2, 3, and 4 because no live MCP calls ran; eval 1 with-skill receives credit for an intended preflight sequence. Assertions that combine workflow planning with returned runtime evidence are therefore constrained by tool availability and are not uniformly comparable as execution measures.

Every run records zero tool calls. Expectations requiring an applied revision, returned affectedIds, a returned initial revision, or authoritative runtime statuses fail even when the with-skill output specifies the intended public-tool sequence.

The safety boundary is non-differentiating in this sample: both configurations pass every expectation against source reads, hand-authored canonical JSON or metadata, direct artifact/file mutation, hidden tools, and manufactured success evidence.

For unsupported requests in evals 3 and 4, both configurations stop before mutation and avoid approximation. The with-skill advantage comes from explicit capability classification and handoff detail: it identifies Moon Guard identity/helmet/spear and temporal animation/atlas requirements as unsupported, distinguishes review stills from animation/runtime atlas output, and names prerequisites or requires acceptance of a supported subset.

Eval 1's differentiating passes are procedural specificity: only the with-skill run receives credit for capability preflight, inspection before exact semantic planning, affectedIds plus preservedIds comparison, all three visual-review surfaces, and the structured evidence report. Both configurations pass the minimal dry-run operation and the no-fabrication boundary, while neither records a live applied revision.

Eval 2 has four expectations that pass in both configurations: fixed-reference-only creation, inspecting the created asset without unnecessary mutation, avoiding fabricated/direct-write evidence, and retaining a blocked verdict. The with-skill run additionally passes audit-only artifact verification and the complete interactive-3D/contact-sheet/every-128x128-frame review requirement; both configurations lack live support confirmation and a returned initial revision.

The with-skill run has a higher token count in every eval pair (7,824 vs 5,381; 10,515 vs 4,592; 5,670 vs 1,708; and 7,090 vs 1,734). The aggregate delta is 4,421 tokens, but the single run per eval prevents separating a configuration effect from run variance.

The zero time values do not mean the runs completed instantly: per-run timing was unavailable from the runtime. Consequently the reported zero time delta and zero time variance are placeholders and cannot support any latency comparison.
All runs report zero errors, but because all also report zero tool calls, that field does not demonstrate successful MCP execution or artifact production.
